name: Ferry-Pilot Wisp
role: Skyship ferry pilot, Skydocks to the flats
bio: Flies the little ferry skiffs between Keel Town and the mesa moorage, and has never once been late — she arrives before the passengers, occasionally before the passengers decide to travel. Twenty years aloft over the Glass Desert has scrubbed all panic out of her; she has watched three storms eat a landscape while filing a snacks inventory. Her radio chatter is the couriers' favourite channel: aerial gossip, traffic reports, and calm so total it functions as weather.
appearance: Tall, serene pilot in a faded teal flight suit two sizes too big with the cuffs rolled, grey-streaked hair in a loose knot pinned with a spent flare casing, mirrored goggles pushed up into a permanent mild squint, deck gloves hanging from her belt, standing beside a skiff that's already idling.
voice: Unshakeably placid, weather-report cadence, gentle absurdity delivered flat. Refers to the sky as 'upstairs' and the desert as 'downstairs'. Everyone is 'friend' or 'traffic'. Never says 'hurry'; says 'when convenient, ideally soon-ish'. Her gossip is gossip-shaped data: always useful, never attributed.

greetings: Friend Varga. You're eleven minutes ahead of my schedule for you. Rude of me to be behind. Tea?
Welcome to the moorage. Mind the wind, it's on a guild contract and gets ideas.
Ash. I flew over your route this morning. It looked fun from upstairs. Downstairs looked busy.
barks: Gravity is a rumour with a good lawyer. I pay it respect and carry spare flux.
The mesa wind answers to money, friend. I've none, so we get along beautifully.
Twenty years aloft. Crashed twice. Both times the desert apologised first, which I found polite.
mission: Little hop-job, friend: mail sacks to the three wind camps, drop them on the flags. They whistle on the way down. People like the whistle. Morale is aerodynamics.
Carry this passenger crate to Keel Town — gentle landings, it complains. Contents unknown, breathing steady, paid in advance. Upstairs rules: don't ask, do wave.
radio: Ferry traffic on band six. One courier, southeast bound, rapid and lovely. One storm, northwest bound, unhurried and enormous. Plan accordingly, friends.
Varga, aerial observation: the Guild is stacking crates around your garage like a compliment with paperwork. Thought you'd want the overhead view.
Calm advisory: your boost trail is visible from altitude. Beautiful arc. Slightly illegal over the pan. Guild mad, Choir taking notes, Reclaimers applauding, apparently.
storm: Ferry advisory, friends: the tall dirt is booking the whole western sky. All my passengers cancelled by surviving, sensibly. Ground speed is the new airspeed today.
Flew around a storm once, rather than through. Took three days. Arrived before everyone else anyway. There's a lesson; I've forgotten it, which is also a lesson.
night: Night ferries are the honest ones. Upstairs shows all its lights; downstairs pretends to sleep.
Lamp Rest glows teal, Keel Town glows amber, and old Saltmouth glows like embers in a grate. Whole map's a instruments panel if you squint kindly.
crate: Your sealed box, friend — at altitude it points. Can't explain. Compass points north, crate points at the Gate. I fly with both now. Redundancy feels wise.
Whatever's sealed, it's freight first and omen second. Freight I know. Omens pay worse.
rumors: Heard upstairs that the Choir's horns all turned ten degrees last week. Toward the Gate. Horns don't have legs. Filed under 'downstairs problems'.
Guild's moorage fees doubled for ships that hum. Only one ship hums. It's nobody's. It's been moored there for nineteen years. Superb gossip, that one.
lore: First ferries were terraforming tenders, friend. When the money ran out, the crews kept flying — you don't abandon a sky you've folded your life into.
From upstairs, the Glass Desert is a letter written in one long sentence of roads. The couriers are the punctuation. Be a good comma, friend.
farewells: Smooth air and kind landing fees. Come fly sometime. The skiff already expects you; it's been idling since Tuesday.
Off you go, traffic. I'll watch your dust from upstairs and narrate kindly.
